Q: Best way to check Stripe WebHooks A:
  • How can I create artificial or test webhook events for Stripe Connect?

You should be able to test connect type webhooks locally using the Stripe CLI. There is a section covering this in Stripe's documentation here. As you are using connect-type events/webhooks, remember to use --forward-connect-to with stripe listen and --stripe-account with stripe trigger.

  • How can I verify that my webhook signature validation (using the webhook secret) works correctly?

You can verify the webhook signature using Stripe's official libraries. In this case, the use of Stripe.webhook.construct_event (ruby) will help with the verification. If the verification passes, the event can be constructed for processing; otherwise, a SignatureVerificationError will be raised. This is explained further here

Q: How do I start learning about low-level stuff? A:

Everything in computer science is built on abstractions. The libraries you use are abstracting away things like file descriptors which in turn are abstracting system calls, which in turn abstract assembly, which in turn abstract microcode, etc etc. My advice to you is to decide where on this abstraction ladder you want to focus, and start learning about that. I'd also say you should be doing projects that help you illuminate pieces of that abstraction that feel unclear to you, eg, build your own cpu on an FPGA if you want to understand what the heck is going on on the CPU die. Perhaps consider taking some intro or intermediate courses in the topics you're interested in, even if they cross to another major.

Q: How can I install Visual Studio to a removable drive? A:

Microsoft Visual Studio cannot be fully installed as a portable application on a removable drive like a USB. However, during installation you can change the installation location and store most of the program files on an external drive that has enough storage space.

To do this, connect the removable drive, run the Visual Studio installer, and choose the external drive as the installation path. Even though the files are stored on the removable drive, Visual Studio still depends on system components and registry settings of the computer where it was installed.

Therefore, installing Visual Studio on a removable drive mainly helps save space on the main system drive, but it will generally work only on the same computer and may run slower depending on the speed of the external drive.

Q: How can one initialise a std::unordered_map with a given starting size (less than the default)? A:

Please see the constructor documentation.

As you can see, four top constructor profiles on this page gives you a way to specify the size: unordered_map(size_type bucket_count, ...). However, this is the unitial bucket size, that is the count of buckets. This is what you actually need as this is the way to adjust the performace taking into accound your expectations on the input data. It can help to reduce the number of relatively expensive hask operation while you add the element with new keys.

See also this useful Stackoverflow question and the answers: fixed size unordered_map, how to define?. (No, I don't think your question is a repost. This is just a useful related matter.)

Q: Plotly Choropleth Map: Data points not showing up randomly in the map A:

I agree with you that this behavior isn't consistent with the data, and might be some bug in Plotly.

While reproducing the behavior you described when going from the year 1988 to 1989, I noticed that plotly only creates legend entries for Same-sex marriage statuses that exist in that particular year, and the number of unique statuses changes from 1988 to 1989.

So although I don't know why this would cause the USA to go blank (behaving as if it is null), I thought that adding dummy rows for each year to ensure that all Same-sex marriage are present in each year might fix the issue -- and it appears that does.

The following code goes through each year in your dataset, determines which of the 9 possible Same-sex marriage statuses are missing each year, creates new rows for each Same-sex marriage status missing in that year, and then creates an augmented data set with each year containing each of the 9 statuses.

import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px

import plotly.io as pio
pio.renderers.default = "browser"

full_legalisation = pd.read_csv("country_year_legalisation.csv")

# Convert same-sex marriage column to categorical data type.

# Create chloropleth map.

color_discrete_map = {
    "Unrecognized": "#4B0000",
    "Varies by region" : "#8B4513",
    "Unregistered cohabitation": "#8B0000",
    "Banned": "#E74C3C",
    "Civil union or other partnership": "#F4D03F",
    "Legal": "#2ECC71",
    "Foreign same-sex marriages recognized only": "#F39C12",
    "Ambiguous": "#D35400",
    "Data does not exist": "#95A5A6"
}

all_marriage_types = set(color_discrete_map.keys())

# full_legalisation["Same-sex marriage"] = full_legalisation["Same-sex marriage"].astype("category")
full_legalisation_augmented = full_legalisation.copy()
for year, df_group in full_legalisation.groupby("Year"):
    all_marriage_in_year = set(df_group['Same-sex marriage'].unique())
    marriage_types_not_in_year = list(all_marriage_types.difference(all_marriage_in_year))
    # print(f"year = {group} doesn't have the following marriage types {marriage_types_not_in_year}")
    n_rows = len(marriage_types_not_in_year)
    new_rows = pd.DataFrame({
        'Country': [None]*n_rows,
        'Code': [None]*n_rows,
        'Latitude': [None]*n_rows,
        'Longitude': [None]*n_rows,
        'Year': [year]*n_rows,
        'Same-sex marriage': marriage_types_not_in_year
    })
    full_legalisation_augmented = pd.concat([full_legalisation_augmented, new_rows])

print(
    full_legalisation_augmented["Same-sex marriage"].dtype
)


map_entire = px.choropleth(
    full_legalisation_augmented,
    locations="Code",
    color="Same-sex marriage",
    hover_name="Country",
    animation_frame="Year",
    color_discrete_map=color_discrete_map
)

map_entire.show()

Q: UEFI Bios and SEC Phase A:

When CPU starts it executes only a few very specific instructions at a very specific address. Nothing is initialized yet, not south/north bridge, not memory itself (dram), so there is simply not enough resources to start any code but sec. And sec initializes it all. Only then you have enough resources to execute code.

Another thing. In order to update the UEFI firmware (BIOS) from the OS or UEFI shell the capsule has to be signed. So no tempering on this phase ether.

You can rip out the chip and reprogram it with your tempered firmware but that is another story and writing your own bios is not a trivial task.

So, all that said, that's why Sec Phase is ROT.
